newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- Dlr/yen volatilities swell, dlr/mark dips.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- Dlr/yen volatilities swell, dlr/mark dips.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options swelled, although they had come off somewhat by afternoon U.S. trading, as the dollar tumbled to fresh six-month lows below 112 yen overnight, traders said.
Shorter dates were particularly well bid because of their higher gamma, which provides quicker price acceleration against spot movements, they added.

"You've had the reaction that everybody knew would occur on a probe of the lows because there were still short-strike and range binary exposures down there," said Alan Revercomb, options strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc.
Strong end-user demand for downside strikes in the past month or so, evidenced in price differential between yen calls and puts, meant many bank dealers were short in downside options, he noted.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal, which had already been sharply skewed for yen calls and stood at 1.2/1.6 point on Friday, widened out further to more than 2.0 today.
Traders were skeptical that such a strong skew or the steep volatility curve inversion could be sustained for long.
"It will flatten out," said a U.S. bank trader in New York. "It should be lower tomorrow."
One-week dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 17.5/18.5 percent in early afternoon U.S. trading after climbing close to 20.0 earlier from about 9.7/10.7 late on Friday.
One-month rose to about 14.3/14.5 percent from 10.3/10.6, and one-year rose a full point to 11.3/11.6.
Although the front end looked very plump, traders appeared cautious about getting short quite yet.

"There's a feeling in the market that the next couple of days can easily bring two-figure (two-yen) ranges to either side," Revercomb said, adding that spot was too close to the lows to be a comfortable nestling area.
The dollar fell to a low of 111.80 yen overnight.

Despite the huge movement in dollar/yen, actual option trade flows were bigger in dollar/mark and other dollar/European currencies, traders noted. They said dollar/mark's pullback from recent highs depressed the front end of the curve, while the back end saw some large selling.
One-month dollar/mark fell about 0.4 point to 9.6/10.0 percent, while one-year came off a touch to 9.4/9.6 percent.
Risk reversals, which had been favoring mark puts for some time, flattened to around par but risk perception had yet to turn around to the dollar's downside, traders said.

"You don't have the same kind of strikes in place and you don't have the same kind of fear about what the downside brings," Revercomb said. But he noted that the five-point spread between front-end implied volatilities for dollar/yen and dollar/mark had to narrow eventually.

That narrowing might come from an easing in dollar/yen volatilities because "it does not take much to move vols from 14.5 to 12.5 percent," but dollar/mark volatilities could become more sensitive to spot's downside as risk reversals shifted toward mark calls and shorts accumulated in the lower strikes, he said.
